submission.natural_language_explanation: L2H0 is a broad retrospective phrase-frame routing head: at each token it attends back (typically weight 0.4-0.97) to the earlier token that opens the current phrase, clause or code line and writes while that phrase completes, so ordinary multi-clause prose reads active-weak and routinely crosses the active line. Strength is graded: strongest (up to max) when the opener is a maximum/minimum-degree marker (superlatives the/-est/best/worst/most including a-most, least, cross-lingual plus/mas forms, and comparatives more/-er...than), peaking on the phrase's head noun or its closing qualifier (in/of/on/ever/never) or the following subject pronoun (I/they/he); moderate on fronted subordinate or adverbial frames (while/when/since/if/after/before), quoted dialogue attribution, fronted wh-frames (Whoever/Which...), bare ever/never continuations, and code lines (strongest on declarations such as #define/private, variable on expression statements); superlatives embedded in adjunct PPs (with the best...) or bare recipe imperatives (Use the deepest pan...) are variable and can read below the line, and reliably below the line are only short single-clause fragments with no such opener and plain lists of bare numbers.

rival_explanations: A generic phrase-completion head that peaks on any mid-length phrase's closing noun or qualifier regardless of its opener, with superlatives merely the strongest case; it predicts plain extended noun-plus-PP frames with no degree word also fire strongly.

A narrow superlative-anchor head that routes only the degree marker itself, with subordinate frames, dialogue tags, bare ever continuations and code lines firing through an unrelated coincidence that should vanish once the superlative is removed.
